Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda =2$ (of multiplicity two) and only one corresponding eigenvector $v,$ the solution of the system is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}\,),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

In our case, 

$$
\lambda =2,\,v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

 
Thus, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}] & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]t{e}^{2t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}) \\  & ={c}_{1}{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}t \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$
lie on the $x\text{-axis}.$ Since ${e}^{2t}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions move toward $\text{infinity}$ in the phase plane as $t\to \infty .$

questions.worked_solution:
Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda =4$ (of multiplicity two) and only one corresponding eigenvector $v,$ the solution of the system is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}\,),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

In our case, 

$$
\lambda =4,\,v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

 
Thus, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}] & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{4t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]t{e}^{4t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{4t}) \\  & ={c}_{1}{e}^{4t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{4t}[\begin{aligned}t \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{4t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$
lie on the $x\text{-axis}.$ Since ${e}^{4t}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions move toward $\text{infinity}$ in the phase plane as $t\to \infty .$

Let's add the solutions to the phase space.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14228295/assets/27e921a76383c4f8a4fc1e81a1febcfad53f330d0e902f4e07578238da33422f.png)

Now, consider solutions of the form
${c}_{2}{e}^{4t}[\begin{aligned}t \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
When ${c}_{2}=1,$ we get the following curve:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=t{e}^{4t} \\ y={e}^{4t}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Computing the coordinates (rounded to two decimal places) of several points on the curve, we get the table below.

| $t$ | $-0.5$ | $0$ | $0.4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $-0.07$ | $0$ | $1.98$ |
| $y$ | $0.14$ | $1$ | $4.95$ |

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda =3$ (of multiplicity two) and only one corresponding eigenvector $v,$ the solution of the system is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}\,),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

In our case, 

$$
\lambda =3,\,v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

 
Thus, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}] & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]t{e}^{3t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}) \\  & ={c}_{1}{e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}t \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$
lie on the $x\text{-axis}.$ Since ${e}^{3t}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions move toward $\text{infinity}$ in the phase plane as $t\to \infty .$

${c}_{2}{e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}t \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
When ${c}_{2}=1,$ we get the following curve:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=t{e}^{3t} \\ y={e}^{3t}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Computing the coordinates (rounded to two decimal places) of several points on the curve, we get the table below.

| $t$ | $-0.5$ | $0$ | $0.5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $-0.11$ | $0$ | $2.24$ |
| $y$ | $0.22$ | $1$ | $4.48$ |
